text: Hello everyone. Ladies and gentlemen,
Russia has lost the Black Sea and Mr.
Putin's greatest goal has failed. Why
do we say that? It is because the Black
Sea and the peninsula are exactly where
this war began and are the reason for
it. But now, Russia's greatest goal is
failing. We all know that historically,
Russia fought against Turkey and the
Ottoman Empire at least a dozen times
to gain control of the Black Sea. And
in fact, Mr. Putin also built the
Sevastopol base on the Crimean
Peninsula. And it was because he wanted
to control the Black Sea that Mr. Putin
seized the Crimean Peninsula in 2014.
After that, Ukraine resolutely
disagreed with that, and because of
that, Mr. Putin attacked Ukraine again.
Thus, it can be said that the beginning
of everything was the Black Sea, but
now Mr. Putin is failing on that very
sea. Next, we will listen to the
analysis by oil tycoon Mikhail
Khodorkovsky. He points out the root
cause of everything and how it evolved
step by step. Putin has lost the Black
Sea, not in the sense that he cannot
find it on a map, but in the sense of
losing control over this strategically
important region for Russia. For access
to the Black Sea and control over the
most important points on the coast,
Russia has fought for centuries.
Starting from the time of Peter the
Great, the Russo-Turkish wars alone,
meaning between Russia and Turkey,
amounted to a dozen conflicts. The
Black Sea is home to the most important
ports and trade routes, as well as a
strategic gateway to the Mediterranean
Sea. Actually, the wars currently
taking place in some respects started
from the Black Sea. It is believed that
Russia must keep the Sevastopol base,
and to do that, it was necessary to
seize Crimea. An independent Ukrainian
state would never agree to lose Crimea,
and that meant the regime in Kyiv
needed to be changed to one that could
be easily controlled. And this mindset
largely led to Russia's invasion in
2022. So far, the war has lasted for
nearly 5 years. The number of deaths on
both sides has reached hundreds of
thousands. While the initial goal was
to dominate the Black Sea, it has led
to the exact opposite result. Putin is
losing the Black Sea. Now, even Putin
himself cannot relax at his favorite
residence in Sochi. In the past, he
visited this place dozens of times each
year, including two mandatory trips for
his own birthday. And for the birthday
of Alina Kabaeva, who is Putin's
mistress or lover. But it has now been
over a year since he last set foot
there. He wanted to gain control over
almost the entire Black Sea, but
instead, he ended up losing control
over his own residence. Not long ago,
Putin visited a Pacific Fleet exercise,
and right on the deck of the missile
cruiser Varyag, he made threatening
statements directed at the collective
West. His statement said that the
authorities of some countries have
recently considered the possibility of
seizing our ships and selling our
looted assets. This is no different
from acts of piracy and looting. And if
this starts being implemented in
reality, we will be forced to respond
proportionately wherever we deem it
necessary and appropriate, at any
location, including within the area of
responsibility of the Pacific Fleet,
meaning anywhere and anytime. It sounds
quite terrifying at first, but to get
on that deck, Putin had to fly all the
way to the distant Far East. It seems
that if you want to make a speech from
the deck of a ship, the Black Sea Fleet
is much closer. Why go to the trouble
of flying nearly 6,000 kilometers? The
answer is very simple: because
Ukrainian drones cannot reach that
Vladivostok area in the Far East. But
here, they can, which means Ukraine is
now dominating the Black Sea region.
Just before the day of Putin's speech,
the Russian fleet failed to repel one
of the largest-scale attacks since the
beginning of the war, aimed at the port
of Novorossiysk. And the port of
Novorossiysk is now, in reality,
Russia's main naval base in the Black
Sea. The attacks on the port of
Novorossiysk have left the US
administration extremely concerned. It
is simply because American companies
have interests in oil infrastructure
and tankers in this region. To protect
their business operations, the
Americans have demanded an end to the
attacks. But they requested it of
Zelensky, not Putin. Strange, isn't it?
It is clearly named the Black Sea Fleet
, yet Russia cannot seem to control
this fleet. How did things end up this
way? At the end of this past July,
Russia celebrated Navy Day. The event
did not go very grandly, and was even
somewhat underwhelming. Before the war,
Vladimir Putin would often ride a
ceremonial motorboat to review the
formation of warships during the naval
parade. But this time, he had to speak
in front of a painted backdrop of a
submarine. Why was that? For some
reason, this year's parade was canceled
just like last year. Putin's sour
expression on Navy Day was entirely
understandable. Because while he was
speaking in front of a painting, a
powerful Ukrainian campaign against
Russia's maritime sector was taking
place on the Sea of Azov and the Black
Sea. In fact, that campaign continues
to this very day. Since the beginning
of July, Ukrainian unmanned sea and
aerial drones. have attacked more than
300 different ships. Operations at
seaports on the Sea of Azov have
effectively been paralyzed. Russian
grain exports from the Azov basin to
the Black Sea have collapsed. This, by
the way, also threatens to cause
problems not only for the budget and
agribusiness in Russia but also for
global food security. Wheat exports at
one point fell to their lowest level in
a decade. In addition, the process of
transporting goods from China has also
been affected, with massive delays.
Grain ship owners have been advised to
install machine guns, rocket launchers,
and mobile air defense missile systems
on their vessels. Insurance companies
now simply refuse to cover war risks
for ships in the Sea of Azov and the
Black Sea. In particular, Russia has
declared its own waters in the Black
Sea to be no longer safe for transport
operations. Russia is also unable to
establish and secure maritime logistics
routes to the Crimean Peninsula because
the Ukrainian military is targeting the
ferry terminals. How could Russian
territorial waters have become so
insecure? And where is the Russian Navy
? Why is the Russian fleet not
protecting the waterways? Why are they
not ensuring control over their own
waters? Before the war, the Russian
Black Sea Fleet's naval forces were
supplemented with three frigates, six
submarines, six small missile ships,
and many other vessels. This shows that
the force was very well-equipped, and
in the full-scale invasion, the Russian
fleet entered the war against a nation
that, in reality, has no fleet of its
own. So, what could have gone wrong
here? At first, things were going quite
smoothly for Putin. Ukraine's Snake
Island was captured, and an amphibious
landing operation was being prepared in
the area near the port of Odessa. But
then the sailors began to suffer losses
from the very first weeks of the war in
early 2022. Following a missile attack
on the port of Berdyansk, one of the
large landing ships sank to the seabed.
And on the night of April 13 into the
early hours of April 14, 2022, the
flagship of the Black Sea Fleet, the
cruiser Moskva, was sunk by Ukrainian
anti-ship missiles, namely the Neptune
missiles. At that very moment, it
became clear that no amphibious
operation to capture Odessa could be
carried out. But no one could have
expected that Ukraine, a country with
absolutely no fleet, would begin a
counter-offensive at sea. In the summer
of 2022, the Russian military, of
course as a "gesture of goodwill,"
withdrew from Snake Island, and shortly
after, the first drone boat attacks
targeted Russian warships. Several
ships were struck right in the port of
Sevastopol. And as we know, the Kerch
Bridge, also known as the Crimean
Bridge, was attacked by drones, and the
Black Sea Fleet headquarters in
Sevastopol was effectively destroyed by
a missile strike. By the end of 2023,
the main forces of the Russian Black
Sea Fleet had withdrawn from Sevastopol
to relocate to Novorossiysk by 2026.
The remnants of the Black Sea Fleet
headquarters building in Sevastopol
were demolished as they were no longer
needed. It is truly symbolic. After all
, it was because of this naval base
that everything started in the first
place. In total, during the war, up to
36 Russian warships, boats, and
submarines have been sunk or heavily
damaged. This accounts for about
one-third of the Black Sea Fleet's
advanced components being taken out of
combat. Ukrainian drones continue to
attack warships in Novorossiysk, in the
Caspian Sea, and even in the Baltic Sea
. Ukrainian attacks are not only
targeting warships and military
facilities but also export
infrastructure. In a recent large-scale
attack on the Russian port of
Novorossiysk, Ukrainian drones and
missiles hit two of the three largest
grain export terminals while damaging
several more Russian warships
helplessly anchored in the port.
Ukraine's success largely stems from
desperation. The country has no fleet,
so they were forced to bet on drones,
missiles, and unmanned surface vessels.
The Ukrainian military has recently
improved its drones and has even
successfully installed air defense
systems on them to counter Russian
helicopters and aircraft. Meanwhile,
the Russian military has been forced to
adopt this experience, and they are now
also launching attacks on commercial
vessels and Ukrainian infrastructure
using missiles, uncrewed boats, and
drones. It is as if there is no fleet
in Russia at all. In 2022, the Russian
fleet controlled nearly 90%of the Black
Sea area in the current theater of war.
But now, according to estimates, this
figure is only 25%. Mostly in the areas
near the Russian coast. The entire role
of the Russian fleet in the current war
is limited to rare cruise missile
launches. Of course, marines are still
fighting on land, and the Russian naval
aviation force is also involved in
intercepting Ukrainian drone attacks.
But in reality, it is not much. At the
end of 2022, Putin proudly declared
that the result of the special military
operation, specifically, the Sea of
Azov, had become an internal Russian
sea. His exact words were about the
long process and the results of the
special military operation. Of course,
this could be a prolonged process. But
you just mentioned that we have
acquired new territories. That is truly
a significant result for Russia. It is
a serious matter. Honestly speaking,
the Sea of Azov has now become an
internal sea of the Russian Federation.
And so, after nearly four years, it
turns out Putin is unable to guarantee
security for this "internal" sea. There
is nothing and no one capable of doing
that. The situation is exactly the same
as in the neighboring Black Sea, where
Putin annexed the Crimean Peninsula.
One reason was to avoid losing the most
important naval base of the Black Sea
Fleet in Sevastopol. They said that if
we lost Sevastopol, we would lose
dominance in the Black Sea. And then a
full-scale invasion of Ukraine broke
out. The cause was largely the fear
that if they didn't do it, the
peninsula would be taken away sooner or
later. So the final result is a war
that has lasted nearly five years
because of these geopolitical illusions
. Russia and Ukraine have paid with the
lives of hundreds of thousands of
people and control of the Black Sea.
The main reason for starting the war
has been lost by Putin himself. It is
truly ironic. Ladies and gentlemen, the
fact that Putin has lost the Black Sea
is not just the words of blogger
Mikhail Khodaryonok, but many Russian
military bloggers have also admitted it
. Here is another one. He is the
well-known reporter Maxim Kalashnikov.
He not only admits that Putin has lost
the Black Sea but also advises
President Putin to end the war before
it is too late. These are the exact
words of Maxim Kalashnikov. He just
said, "No matter what, the end is now
very, very close." Over the past four
and a half years, the Russian economy
has been devastated and exhausted. Do
you remember? We once had many
opportunities to achieve a swift
victory. But one opportunity after
another was missed. Or rather, they
were let go one after another. Although
, to be precise, Ukraine is currently
in a difficult situation, they have
external support. By the end of this
year, they will receive 37 billion
dollars. Just calculate that, it's the
funding for the upcoming months of
October, November, and December.
Meanwhile, the Russian Federation does
not have that. We have currently lost
our own foreign exchange reserves. And
domestic tax revenue is no longer
enough to compensate. No matter the
circumstances, right now we need to
find a way out of this war. And ideally
, with a victory. Because if not, what
we will get in return are just ruins or
the remnants of cities like Sloviansk
and Kramatorsk. However, the reality is
that we are not actually fighting
Ukraine, right? Ukraine only plays the
role of a killing machine. This is a
mistaken perception held by many
Russians. Even those who follow this
war closely all consider Ukraine to be
merely a tool of the West, of Europe.
As for the Russian Federation, Ukraine
is just a tool in the hands of a much
more powerful enemy. It is clear that
we are facing all of Europe and the
West. And from Europe's perspective,
everything is still going on quite
normally. They want to cause a rift
between Great Russians and Little
Russians. They consider Ukrainians to
be Little Russians. They have
successfully caused that division. They
are preventing the most developed,
prosperous, and wealthy territory,
which is Ukraine, from being annexed
into the Russian Federation. Yes, they
did not allow that to happen. Places
that just yesterday still held many
factories, enterprises, and cities. Now
are nothing but desolate ruins. Now
those regions are no longer a source of
strength, but have effectively become a
massive financial burden for
reconstruction. This means that not
only have we failed to overcome the
consequences of the Soviet collapse,
but we have actually deepened them.
From the perspective of the West—the
very West we are actually fighting
through the Ukraine buffer zone, or in
other words, through a proxy war in
Ukraine—things are playing out
exactly as they want. This means that
an enormous amount of money and
resources that could have been invested
in the industrialization of the Russian
Federation. To resolve the demographic
crisis, address housing issues, or
eradicate poverty in Russia, all of it
has now been completely swallowed up by
this war. I am sure you can understand
for yourselves how difficult the
current situation is. Indeed, they have
kicked us out of our own geopolitical
sphere of influence. Even in the Black
Sea, they have almost completely cut
off our maritime routes. He admits that
Russia is losing the Black Sea and has
caused a deeply profound trauma for the
poor working class in Russia. Do you
remember some Bandera-affiliated
elements once declaring that they must
ensure that when hearing the phrase "we
can repeat it." Every Russian citizen
should tremble and think, absolutely
not. God forbid that happens, and
indeed, that trauma has already been
created. Therefore, this is his message
to President Putin. Do not make the
situation any worse. Whether cities
like Sloviansk or Kramatorsk fall into
our hands or not, that alone brings
complexity, and a crisis has certainly
already been shaped at this stage. And
if we get too carried away with a
strategy of not touching the enemy's
leadership while punishing the common
people below, we could very well suffer
retaliation. Because we ourselves also
have many fatal weaknesses. Ladies and
gentlemen, today we explore another
crucial aspect of this war, which is
the Black Sea. But in your opinion, if
Mr. Putin were to lose the Black Sea,
lose control over the port of
Sevastopol and the Crimean Peninsula,
would he agree to end this war? Because
as you have seen, Ukraine has
successfully developed such naval
capabilities. Would Mr. Putin truly be
willing to accept that? We invite you
to please leave your thoughts in the
comments section below. Thank you, and
I look forward to seeing you in the
next program. Thank you all very much.
